reasons: Classification is correct: the sole liability clause (p0077) caps only TrueLink — and only for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 — while Client's liability, including under the broad Section 12a indemnity, is uncapped. That is expressly walk-away territory under LOL-CAP and fails the fallback (mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs), so a deviation with a redline is warranted.

Redline reaches the playbook position: it makes the cap mutual and of general application, uses the greater of 12 months' compensation paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds the Excluded Claims sentence (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), adds the mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, and confirms Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap — tracking the model language while reusing the clause's existing 'compensation for hosting and support services' basis and ALL-CAPS style.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.805 changed-character ratio) is expected here: mutualising a one-sided cap, changing the basis and inserting carve-outs cannot be done without rewriting the single capitalised sentence; the surrounding indemnity section is left untouched.

Comment is accurate, on-tone and prefix-compliant: it states what changed, why (only TrueLink capped, Client unlimited), that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap, and offers the straight 12-month mutual fee cap fallback.

Minor, non-fatal points to sanity-check rather than blockers: the new cross-references ('indemnification obligations under Section 12', 'compensation due under Section 5') should be confirmed against the document's numbering, and the fee basis remains limited to hosting and support compensation rather than all fees; also note the rationale stresses Client's uncapped indemnity while the redline (per playbook) keeps indemnities uncapped for both parties, so the net benefit to Client comes from capping its other liabilities.
